title: ASP.NET Core: Auth in a Nutshell

scenes.say: Who gets through your API gates? How does ASP.NET Core decide who’s in or out?

scenes.label: AuthN
scenes.sub: Authentication checks who the user is.
scenes.say: First up, authentication. That’s how the app checks who someone actually is.

scenes.label: AuthZ
scenes.sub: Authorization checks what they can do.
scenes.say: Next, authorization. That’s how you decide what they can do once they're in.
You set up token authentication with JWT, then add policies or roles to lock down access.
Always run authentication before authorization middleware. Otherwise, the app won’t know who’s making the request.

scenes.question: What happens if you swap the order?
scenes.right: Authorization fails because no user is identified.
scenes.say: Here’s a common trap: if you run authorization before authentication, nobody gets access. The app doesn’t know who you are!
